attempts.raw_response: The primary component, designated WDC 1407A, is estimated to have a mass of about 73 Jupiter masses, placing it near the boundary between the heaviest brown dwarfs and the lightest stars. Its companion, WDC 1407B, has an estimated mass of approximately 65 Jupiter masses. Both objects are classified as L-type dwarfs, with effective temperatures around 2,000 and 1,900 kelvin, respectively. The system is located roughly 34 light-years from Earth and is estimated to be between 500 million and one billion years old. Astronomers expect that continued monitoring of the pair's orbital motion will refine mass estimates and improve understanding of substellar formation.

pair.prefix:
Astronomers suspected the brown dwarf was a binary system upon follow-up observations showing it had an unusual infrared spectrum, but its binarity was not confirmed until the James Webb Space Telescope resolved the system's components in high-resolution NIRCam imaging in September 2022, with its results published in March 2023.

The two components orbit their system barycenter approximately every 7 years and are separated 0.97 astronomical units from each other, which is slightly less than the distance between the Sun and Earth.
